item.title: The Red Ink That Left a Shadow — Synchrotron XRF/XRD Mapping of Tebtunis Temple Papyri, Hematite Strokes With Lead-Phosphate Coffee-Ring Halos & Roman Bronze Inkwell Corrosion
item.description: Synchrotron archaeometry of ancient Egyptian medical/ritual papyri (#39): Christiansen et al.'s (2020 PNAS) sub-micrometer XRF/XRD/FTIR mapping of 12 Tebtunis temple-library fragments showing hematite red-ocher pigment surrounded by sub-visible lead-phosphate/sulfate coffee-ring margins and lead palmitate, copper-bearing soot in Pathyris/Tebtunis black inks (2017), and Sibilia et al.'s (2021) Este Roman bronze inkwell distinguishing carbon-gum ink from container-corrosion cerussite (84% of Pb) and malachite.

item.title: The Water the City Kept — Tikal Maya Corriental Crystalline Quartz & Zeolite Filtration, Cinnabar Mercury & Cyanobacterial eDNA Across Urban Reservoirs
item.description: Ancient urban hydrology and geoarchaeology at Classic Maya Tikal (#32): Scarborough et al.'s (2012) reservoir excavation framework, Tankersley et al.'s (2020) discovery of imported volcanogenic clinoptilolite/mordenite zeolites and macrocrystalline quartz in Corriental sediments, Lentz et al.'s (2020) cinnabar-derived mercury and Planktothrix cyanobacterial eDNA in central palace reservoirs, and 2021 arboreal sediment eDNA.

item.title: The Grave With Two Calendars — Repton Viking Charnel Deposit, Anglo-Saxon Silver Coin Hoard (873–874 CE) vs. Bone Collagen Radiocarbon & Marine Reservoir Correction
item.description: Archaeometric resolution of the Repton Viking Great Army charnel deposit: why five silver pennies in Grave 529 dated the burial to 873–874 CE while uncalibrated terrestrial bone collagen 14C dates appeared centuries older, and how Jarman et al. (2018) combined delta-13C/delta-15N dietary paleodiet reconstruction with marine reservoir correction (Heaton et al. 2020 Marine20) to reconcile the numismatic and radiocarbon calendars.

item.title: The First Anatomists of Speech — 430,000-Yr Ear Bones, Neanderthal Hyoids & Shanidar Care
item.description: Reconstructs Middle Pleistocene speech acoustics from Sima de los Huesos ossicles (2–4 kHz), Kebara 2's hyoid, FOXP2, and Shanidar 1's decades of social survival.

item.title: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
item.description: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

item.title: Twenty-Seven Body Parts to Apothecary Grains — How Language Built Number & Dosing
item.description: Traces embodied human numeracy from Oksapmin 27-locus body counting and Paleolithic bone tallies to Sumerian bullae and life-or-death ancient apothecary metrology.

item.title: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology
item.description: Walks into the 4th-century BCE abaton at Epidaurus—translating the carved Iamata stelae alongside archaeological scalpels and modern PAG opioid/CB1 imaging.

item.title: The 140 BCE Shipwreck Medicine Chest — Spectroscopy of the Pozzino Roman Eye-Tablets
item.description: Dives onto the 140–120 BCE Relitto del Pozzino off Tuscany to chemically analyze intact 2,150-year-old Roman zinc ophthalmic tablets alongside cataract couching.

item.title: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
item.description: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

item.title: Neolithic Flint Drills & Maya Jade Smiles — 9,000 Years Against Trigeminal Dental Agony
item.description: Why tooth pulp pain is uniquely excruciating (Brännström A-delta hydrodynamics), 7000 BCE Mehrgarh bow-drilled molars, antibacterial Maya jade cements, and henbane.

item.title: Evolved for the Impossible — Bajau 13-Min Divers, Denisovan Sherpas & 13.7 °C Survival
item.description: How genetic evolution (Bajau PDE10A giant spleens, Denisovan Sherpa EPAS1) and Q10 thermodynamics (Anna Bågenholm's 13.7 °C resuscitation) shield the 20W human brain.

item.title: Diagnosing the Dead — Can Ancient DNA & Modern Medicine Decode Cuneiform & Athens?
item.description: Stages the fierce debate between dental-pulp ancient DNA paleogenomics and medical historians warning against retrospective diagnostic anachronism.

item.title: Strasbourg 1518 & the Dancing Plagues — Rye Ergot Alkaloids vs. Mass Motor Contagion
item.description: Debates Claviceps purpurea ergot alkaloid pharmacology vs. famine-and-curse predictive dissociative trance in the July 1518 Strasbourg Dancing Plague.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Toe That Had to Walk — Ancient Egyptian Wooden & Cartonnage Prosthetic Great Toes, TT95A Bioarchaeology & Gait Lab Biomechanics
item.description: Bioarchaeological and biomechanical evaluation of the Cairo wooden toe (JE 100016a from TT95A) and British Museum Greville Chester cartonnage toe (EA29996): healed first-MTP amputation, refitting wear marks, and Finch et al. (2012) Salford gait-lab kinematics and plantar pressure mat experiments.

item.title: The Lens That Never Left the Eye — Ancient Cataract Couching in Celsus & Sushruta, α/γ-Crystallin Optics, Aphakic Refraction & Survey Outcomes
item.description: From Celsus and Sushruta's descriptions of cataract couching to alpha/gamma-crystallin short-range order, zonular lysis, why a displaced lens restores light transmission while leaving the eye ~+10 D aphakic, and the 249-eye Nigerian survey separating presenting vs. pinhole-corrected visual acuity.

item.title: The Leaf That Came Out Whole — Chimpanzee Rough-Leaf Swallowing, Vernonia Pith, Rakus Wound Care & Neolithic Durrington Coprolites
item.description: Comparative evidence ledger across animal self-medication and paleoparasitology: physical Oesophagostomum worm expulsion via folded Aspilia leaves at Mahale, bitter Vernonia amygdalina sesquiterpene lactones, orangutan Fibraurea wound application, and fecal sterol/aDNA authentication of Neolithic Durrington Walls coprolites.

item.title: The Glue, the Chew, and the Wound — Neolithic Syltholm Birch Pitch, Betulin Triterpenes, Ancient Oral Metagenomes & Epidermolysis Bullosa Trials
item.description: From a 5,700-year-old chewed birch bark pitch at Syltholm (Denmark) yielding a complete human genome and oral microbiome to GC-MS betulin/lupeol biomarkers, in vitro agar disk diffusion limits, and the Phase III EASE clinical trial of standardized birch triterpenes in epidermolysis bullosa.

item.title: The Tooth That Kept the Tool Marks — Neanderthal Molar Grooves, Villabruna Caries Scraping, Mehrgarh Bow-Drills & Lonche Beeswax
item.description: Scanning electron microscopy, micro-CT, and FTIR spectroscopy of prehistoric worked teeth: Neanderthal interproximal toothpick grooves, Upper Paleolithic Villabruna carious lesion scraping, Neolithic Mehrgarh flint bow-drilled molars, and the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling.

item.title: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H037 (DXA Bone Densitometry & Projection Artifacts): how two-energy X-ray attenuation integrates all mineral along the beam path, why an L1 vertebral compression fracture and abdominal aortic calcification produced a high anteroposterior lumbar reading (Gupta et al. 2021), iodinated contrast (+3.8 to -1.5 T-score) and vertebral cement exclusions (+7.7 to -2.6 T-score, White et al. 2025), person-level vs. vertebra-level osteophyte and fracture comparisons in 96 women (Paiva et al. 2002), and the 2023 ISCD Adult Official Positions.

item.title: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT
item.description: Bioarchaeological and analytical investigation of prehistoric dentistry: concentric flint drill striations in Neolithic Mehrgarh molars (Coppa et al. 2006), Upper Paleolithic Villabruna and Riparo Fredian cavities, and synchrotron FTIR/radiocarbon verification of the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling (Bernardini et al. 2012).

item.title: The Seasons Inside a Tooth — Neanderthal Enamel Retzius Lines, Oxygen Isotopes, Barium Nursing Traces & Lead Bands
item.description: High-resolution laser-ablation and SHRIMP microprobe reading of Neanderthal teeth (Smith et al. 2018): daily enamel cross-striations, seasonal oxygen-18 cycles, barium/calcium nursing transitions, and acute wintertime lead exposure bands.

item.title: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
item.description: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

item.title: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
item.description: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

item.title: What the Ice Kept in the Skin — Ötzi the Iceman's 61 Soot Tattoos, Multispectral Reflectance, Pazyryk Mummies & Therapeutic vs. Symbolic Puncturing
item.description: Non-invasive multispectral photographic mapping and histological analysis of preserved ancient skin tattoos in glacial and permafrost mummies (Samadelli et al. 2015 on Ötzi's 61 tattoos across 19 anatomical groups), Raman carbon-soot chemistry, and testing the joint-degeneration acupuncture hypothesis.

item.title: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
item.description: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

item.title: The Last Meal in the Bog — Tollund Man's Gut Contents, Barley-Flax-Weed Gruel, Whipworm Eggs & Forensic Reconstruction
item.description: Multi-proxy forensic re-analysis of Tollund Man's large-intestinal contents (Nielsen et al. 2021): plant macrofossils, pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, ancient DNA, proteins, lipids, Trichuris trichiura eggs, and why threshing waste was intentionally added.

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis

item.title: The Scroll That Stayed Rolled — Virtual Unwrapping from En-Gedi's Metal-Bearing Ink (Seales 2016) to Herculaneum Carbon Ink (Parker 2019) & Complete Surface Reading of PHerc. 1667 & Philodemus's On Gods Book 8
item.description: X-ray micro-CT virtual unwrapping and machine-learned carbon-ink detection in carbonized ancient scrolls: Seales et al.'s (2016) reading of Leviticus inside the charred En-Gedi scroll, Parker et al.'s (2019) 3D voxel ink classification on Herculaneum fragment PHerc.
